questions: Have you noticed shaking or trembling in your hands?
Is the shaking worse when you are using your hands or holding something?
Does one hand shake more than the other?
Have you noticed stiffness or slowness of movement?
Have you had any problems with balance or walking?
Do you have involuntary jerking or writhing movements of your arms, legs, or face?
Do you have neck pain or involuntary turning or tilting of your head?
Have you ever had a stroke or other neurological illness?
Does the shaking occur mainly when your hands are completely at rest?
Does the shaking lessen or stop when you reach for or hold an object?
Does alcohol temporarily reduce the shaking?
Does anyone in your family have a similar tremor?
Are you taking medicines such as lithium, valproate, stimulants, or bronchodilators?
Have you had symptoms of an overactive thyroid, such as weight loss, heat intolerance, sweating, or a racing heartbeat?
Does the tremor vary noticeably in speed or severity during the day?
Can you briefly stop or suppress the tremor if you concentrate on doing so?
Did the tremor begin after a stressful event, emotional upset, injury, or illness?
Do you have other unexplained neurological symptoms, such as episodes of weakness, numbness, abnormal walking, or non-epileptic seizures?
orders: Bedside tremor examination with the patient extending both arms, writing a sentence, drawing an Archimedes spiral, and performing a finger-to-nose test, while assessing tremor frequency, regularity, distractibility, and entrainment during contralateral finger tapping.
served: distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side)
entrainment testing (tap to an externally paced rhythm)
